name: DeepSeek API token pricing (serverless, off-peak vs peak, 2026-10-04 list price)
price_basis: USD per 1M TOKENS, LIST PRICE, observed 2026-10-04. Two models, each with an OFF-PEAK and a PEAK rate, off-peak being exactly half of peak. deepseek-flash (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash): cache-hit input $0.003 off-peak / $0.006 peak; cache-MISS input $0.15 off-peak / $0.30 peak; output $0.60 off-peak / $1.20 peak. deepseek-v4-pro (DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813): cache-hit $0.022/$0.044; cache-miss $0.66/$1.32; output $1.98/$3.96. price_usd = flash cache-miss input, off-peak. Peak hours are 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC Monday-Friday excluding Chinese public holidays; every other hour including all weekends and all Chinese public holidays is off-peak. Concurrency limits quoted on the same page: 2500 for flash, 500 for v4-pro.
notes: This is the only provider in this set with a TIME-OF-DAY PRICE, and it is a 2x swing that no naive cost model captures. A workload that is latenct-tolerant enough to run at night pays half; the same tokens on a weekday morning cost double. For a batch or eval pipeline, schedule against the peak windows rather than averaging them. Second structural point: cache-hit input at $0.003 per 1M is 50x cheaper than cache-miss at $0.15, which makes prompt caching the dominant lever here by a wider margin than at any other provider in this set (Anthropic's best cache read is 40x its input; Google's cache storage is charged per hour instead). Any DeepSeek bill that does not report a cache-hit share is hiding the main cost driver. DeepSeek publishes no GPU hourly rate and no region list.
